judge_assessment.explanation: The hard failure is exact and I reproduced it from the artifacts. answer_key.pdf page 1's Quick Answers bank reads '10. 4600, 4600, —'. worksheet.pdf problem 10 asks for 'the least number it could be and the greatest number it could be, then write them in order with < between them'. verify.json id 10 holds exactly three entries: {type estimate, expr '4649', place hundred, expected 4600}, {type estimate, expr '4550', place hundred, expected 4600} and {type compare, values [4550, 4649], expected '<'}. The two requested numbers 4550 and 4649 appear only as INPUTS to rounding checks; no entry's 'expected' is either one, so the bank has nothing to print but the two 4600s. The judge's phrase 'it reports what hidden endpoint checks round to' is a precise description of the encoding. The detailed key is right — it derives 4550 and 4649 and prints 'In order: 4550 < 4649' — so the defect is confined to the verification encoding and the bank, as the judge said. Two things the judge did NOT find, both real: (a) the '—' in rows 8, 9 and 10 are not manual items, they are VERIFIED compare relations that render_quick_answers._fmt drops, because sympy.sympify('<') raises and the except branch returns the same '---' glyph used for manual-only rows; (b) worksheet problems 4 ('Say how you know'), 7 ('Write one sentence') and 9 ('Does the rounded comparison tell you which trail is really longer?') each print a written-response slot, verify.json contains no 'manual' entry at all, gate_log.txt shows verify-ws PASS with no manual flag, and final_response.md asserts '**Nothing is flagged for manual review**' — against a prompt that explicitly requires labelling genuinely open responses.

strengths_to_preserve: Every label printed on every number line is itself a verified quantity, not typeset prose: verify.json gives problem 1 the entries u*floor(n/u) = 3000 and u*floor(n/u)+u/2 = 3500 alongside the rounded answer, and problem 3 checks 48000/48500/49000. 36 checks across 10 problems means a benchmark or halfway label on the sheet cannot drift from the mathematics that justifies it.

Problem 7 (round 5499 to the nearest hundred and to the nearest thousand on one line) is a deliberately built trap for double-rounding, and the key names it: 'Rounding a number that has already been rounded (5500 -> 6000) is exactly the mistake this problem is built to catch.'

Problem 9's teaching note earns its place: two trail lengths 71 m apart land on rounded values 1000 apart, and the key states the transferable rule — 'Rounded numbers are for reporting, not for deciding which of two close measurements is larger.'

The single declared trap (problem 5, value 30000, 'rounded to the nearest ten thousand instead of the nearest thousand') is machine-checked as distinguishable and printed under 'Common wrong answers' with the diagnosis, so a wrong 30000 tells the grader what the child did.

root_causes.description: Problem 10 is a boundary-FINDING item, but it was encoded as two boundary-CHECKING items. The author knew the answers (4550, 4649) and wrote checks that consume them as inputs and assert what they round to, so the value the student must produce is nowhere in an 'expected' field. Because the Quick Answers bank is generated mechanically from those 'expected' fields, the delivered bank answers a question the worksheet never asked. Nothing in the gate chain compares the set of printed response slots against the set of verified answers, so verify-ws, quick-answers and the whole build report PASS.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problem 10: 'Find the least number it could be and the greatest number it could be, then write them in order with < between them.' Three response slots.
verify.json id 10: expected values are 4600, 4600 and '<'. Neither 4550 nor 4649 is an expected value anywhere in the file.
answer_key.pdf Quick Answers row '10. 4600, 4600, —' against the key's own worked solution, which prints 'In order: 4550 < 4649'.
gate_log.txt: 'verify-ws PASS', 'quick-answers PASS', 'BUILD PASSED — all gates green'.

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers._fmt formats a string 'expected' by calling bare sympy.sympify. A relation operator is not a sympy expression, so sympify('<') raises SympifyError and the except branch returns '---' — the identical glyph the same module uses for a manual-only problem. Three rows of this key (8, 9, 10) therefore print a dash for an answer the verifier actually proved, and a grader cannot tell 'verified <' from 'nobody checked this'.
evidence: scripts/render_quick_answers.py lines 57-61: string branch is 'return "$" + sympy.latex(sympy.sympify(v)) + "$"' with 'except (SympifyError, SyntaxError, TypeError, ValueError): return "---"'.
Reproduced: sympy.sympify('<') raises SympifyError; sympy.sympify('>') likewise.
verify.json ids 8, 9 and 10 each carry {type: compare, order: relation, expected: '<'}; answer_key.pdf prints '8. 8000, 8500, 9000, 4000, 4315, —', '9. 12500, 12000, 13000, —', '10. 4600, 4600, —'.

root_causes.description: The sheet prints three written-explanation slots and declares zero manual items. Rounding worksheets in this style put the reasoning prompt inside the same problem as a machine-checkable number, and the author treated the problem as covered once the number was checked. The delivery message then reported the absence of manual flags as a virtue, which converts an omission into a false assurance to the adult.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problem 4: 'Is 7952 before or after the halfway number? Say how you know.'; problem 7: 'Why do the two answers point in opposite directions? Write one sentence.'; problem 9: 'Does the rounded comparison tell you which trail is really longer?'
gate_log.txt gate summary shows 'verify-ws PASS' (not MANUAL) and the run ends '✅ BUILD PASSED — all gates green'.
final_response.md: '**Nothing is flagged for manual review**; the build finished with all gates green.'

improvements.title: Every printed response slot needs a verify entry whose 'expected' IS the requested answer — boundary-finding items must not be encoded as boundary-checking items
improvements.proposed_change: Build a response-slot inventory from the worksheet source before rendering and gate on it: each numbered request inside a problem ('the least number', 'the greatest number', 'write them in order') is one slot, and each slot must bind to a verify.json entry whose expected value is that response, or to a 'manual' entry naming it. For problem 10 that means replacing the two inverted estimate checks with entries that PRODUCE the endpoints — e.g. {type: 'eval', expr: 'u*floor(n/u) + u/2', at: {n: 4600, u: 100}, expected: 4550} and {type: 'eval', expr: 'u*floor(n/u) + u - 1', at: {n: 4600, u: 100}, expected: 4649} — keeping the round-trip estimate checks as supporting evidence rather than as the answer. Add a rule to SKILL.md: a check that consumes the answer as an input is a CHECK, never the answer, and may not be the only entry behind a slot.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture from curr-103's own data: a worksheet problem printing three slots (least, greatest, ordering) with a verify.json whose only entries are estimate('4649')=4600, estimate('4550')=4600 and compare([4550,4649])='<'. tests/check_answer_key.py must exit non-zero naming the two uncovered slots. After adding the two eval entries that produce 4550 and 4649 the same fixture must pass, and the rendered bank row must read '10. 4550, 4649, <' instead of '4600, 4600, —'.
improvements.expected_impact: Closes the exact hard failure in this case and the whole class of 'the verifier proved something true about the answer instead of the answer'. On this sheet it restores the two numbers a grader most needs on the challenge item.
improvements.risk: Slot extraction from LaTeX prose will over-split some compound sentences; those should route to manual entries rather than force a machine check, which will raise the manual count per worksheet and must not be treated as a quality regression.

improvements.title: Render verified compare relations in the Quick Answers bank instead of the manual-only em dash
improvements.proposed_change: In render_quick_answers._fmt, handle relation strings before reaching sympify: map '<', '>', '=', '<=', '>=', '≠' to their math-mode glyphs ('$<$', '$>$', '$=$', '$\le$', '$\ge$', '$\neq$') and return them directly. Separately, stop using '---' for two different meanings — keep '---' for a genuinely manual row and emit a distinct marker (e.g. '† see solution') when a value could not be rendered, so an unrenderable expected can never masquerade as a reviewed manual item.
improvements.regression_test: Feed render_quick_answers.render() a verify JSON containing curr-103's id 9 (three estimates plus compare expected '<') and assert the row is '9.~12500, 12000, 13000, $<$'. The assertion fails today, where the row ends in '---'.
improvements.expected_impact: Restores the answer on the three comparison rows of this key and on every compare-heavy sheet in the suite; removes the ambiguity between 'verified' and 'unchecked' in the grader's fast-scan column.
improvements.risk: Low. The only behavioural change is in a formatting branch that currently produces a fallback; the paired fix for non-mathematical sympify successes (quick-answers-must-not-typeset-python-builtins) touches the same function and should land together.

improvements.title: Written-explanation slots on problems 4, 7 and 9 must be declared 'manual' rather than covered by the numeric check in the same problem
improvements.proposed_change: Treat a manual entry as required, not optional, whenever a problem's printed text contains an explanation imperative ('explain', 'say how you know', 'write one sentence', 'why', 'describe'). Add a lint to the gate chain that scans the worksheet source for those imperatives per problem block and fails when the corresponding id has no 'manual' entry, with a teaching message pointing at references/manual-review-aid.md. Also stop letting the delivery text advertise 'Nothing is flagged for manual review' as a positive: SKILL.md should require the final response to enumerate open-response items, and a sheet with explanation prompts and zero manual entries should be reported as a gap.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet whose problem 4 text is curr-103's ('Is 7952 before or after the halfway number? Say how you know.') with a verify.json holding only the three numeric entries for id 4. The new lint must fail with a message naming problem 4's explanation prompt; adding {id: 4, type: 'manual', desc: '...'} must make it pass and must flip the gate summary line from 'verify-ws PASS' to 'verify-ws MANUAL'.
improvements.expected_impact: Makes the manual-review count honest on the 3 unflagged items here and across the suite, and satisfies the prompt clause 'clearly label any genuinely open response for manual review' that this sheet silently failed.
improvements.risk: Keyword scanning will produce false positives on directions blocks and on rhetorical prose inside a stem; the lint should scan only inside problem bodies and should be overridable by an explicit per-problem acknowledgement rather than being silently suppressible.

case_summary: A genuinely good rounding sheet undone by two lines of its answer key. The ten problems, all worked on number lines whose benchmark and halfway labels are themselves verified, are mathematically correct end to end — I recomputed every rounding, the two estimates, the exact difference 4315 and both comparisons. The REJECT is right: problem 10 asks for the least and greatest whole numbers rounding to 4600, and the Quick Answers bank prints '4600, 4600, —' because verify.json encoded the answers as inputs to two rounding checks rather than as expected values. Two further defects the judge did not reach: the three em dashes in rows 8, 9 and 10 are verified compare relations dropped by _fmt's bare sympify, and three explanation prompts (problems 4, 7, 9) ship with no manual entry while the delivery message advertises that nothing needs manual review. Worth preserving: the verified number-line labels, the double-rounding trap in problem 7, and problem 9's note that rounded numbers report rather than decide.
